Championship at Halton on March 18th with a time of 1:39:39. Winner was Hart in 1:38:02.
Seniors:North 3rd,North 15th,Hart 23rd,Fairclough 24th,Dabbs 29th,O'Hara 51st. Juniors:Bicourt 23rd,Cocks 51st,Hampshire 53rd,Morrison 119th---Belgrave 7th.
A disappointing championship with 9 retirements, including Kerr, Hart and Pat Newell. Gerry North moved away in the latter stages of the race, doing just enough to win.
However, fine packing gave BELGRAVE the team race, our four scorers being 3rd Kerr 9:12, 4th O'Hara 9:15, 6th Gerry North 9:20, 8th Hart 9:29.
(Photo by Ron Linstead)--The Southern field after half a mile. Ringed athletes (l.to r.)are, Black, O'Hara,Fairclough,Hart, Steer,Thresher.
Others to be'pulled' were Paddick (RSC) and Hart, the Welsh champion. Bob Farley, who is showing good form once again, rose to the occasion and scored in our team in 34th place.
Because of this we attempted to do the same this year but finished one place further down in each event; both teams being affected by injuries and Thresher, Hart and Reilly all being unavailable.
Thirteen Belgravians made the journey but of the first-liners only Bicourt (4th) and Major (6th) and Hart (26th) appeared - the latter obviusly having an "easy", rounding up our supporting runners.

In the "longs" a buoyant mood is apparent with STEER, DABBS, MANN And HART Corp. moving steadily forward. The index, rallying towards the close was depressed on the news that HERCULES was making a bid for SATCHELL.
The team that eventually took part was but a shadow of our full strength with names such as Fairclough, Hart, O'Hara, Steer, Thresher and Whewell missing from the line up.
Of last year's team, Dabbs, Hart, Bicourt, Thorpe, Black and Reilly were absent their places being taken by Buxton, Williams, Geoff North, Whewell, Major and Kerr.

These two, plus Hart and Fairclough, were missing this time so Whewell and O'Hara were favourites to gain the place medals. After the first lap the expected medallists still had the close company of Dabbs, Major and Bicourt with O'Hara towing them along at a snappy pace.

I wonder what Thresher, Fairclough, Major, Bicourt, O'Hara, Hart, Dabbs, Steer etc. think of that. Agreed that the North brothers, Dance, Whewell, Williams, Kerr and others have played parts of varying degrees in our success but they joined us on moving to London because they had to change their club.

Gilt edge Hart, Duquemin, Middleton, Major, Kerr and Martin continue as the backbone of our economy. Whilst high flyers Bent and Thresher continue to excite, Dull spots occurred with results from Hilton, C.
We do not have a good record in the "Finchley" but with a first class quartet in Mann, O'Connor, Hart and Dabbs we should put matters right this year.
For the short legs Hart, O'Connor, Dance and Diprose look well placed, with the last two places to be scrambled for by Bicourt, O'Hara, Piotrowski, Cross and Kerr.

This race produced a good turnout of about fifty runners but notable absentees were the North brothers, Bicourt and Hart.
